headline: Rackspace Spot breach via compromised credentials exposed customer Kubernetes secrets
summary: Rackspace says attackers used compromised credentials to breach its Rackspace Spot cloud platform. They deployed unauthorized workloads and accessed Kubernetes secrets in customer clusters.

headline: FBI investigates apparent breach of national criminal justice database
summary: The FBI is looking into what appears to be a hack of a national law enforcement database that it runs. A single source, citing AP, reported the investigation. The source does not give details on scope, the actor or the method.

headline: FBI reportedly suffers second breach in two months, this time involving NCIC police database
summary: Reports say FBI systems were breached again, less than two months after an earlier incident. This time the reported target is the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which local, state and federal law enforcement use to share information. The source does not confirm the scope, the method or who is responsible.

headline: Weekly recap: Optimizely platform abused to plant malware on 178 orgs; OpenJDK Java4Shell flaw hard to exploit
summary: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's web experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customer websites, affecting 178 organisations including BBC, CNN and Zoom, according to the company. The recap also covers CVE-2026-114938, an OpenJDK Base64 decoder memory-corruption flaw whose exploitation reportedly depends on specific CPUs.

headline: Microsoft reports breach after flaw in Entra Connect Health exploited to access tenant data
summary: Microsoft says it suffered a data breach after attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Entra Connect Health service. The attackers got unauthorized access to customers' administrator email addresses and tenant configuration information. No CVE, scope or attribution was given in the source.

headline: Researchers show Ghostscript sandbox escape enabling RCE through crafted file uploads
summary: pwn.ai showed that a now-patched Ghostscript flaw lets a crafted file escape the sandbox and run commands on servers that process uploads. Many Linux applications call Ghostscript indirectly to convert PDFs, PostScript files and images. No in-the-wild exploitation was reported.

headline: Months-long prompt theft found at three AI inference providers; OpenRouter drops them
summary: Dragos reported that attackers stole data from inside three AI inference providers for months without the providers noticing. Some of the stolen requests were marked Zero Data Retention. OpenRouter removed the three providers from its routing pool.

headline: BADBOX botnet on Android TV boxes resumes large-scale ad fraud after last year's disruptions
summary: BADBOX malware, found on many generic Android TV boxes, is again running large-scale ad fraud after being disrupted last year. Its traffic reportedly peaks at around 40 billion ad requests a day.

headline: mod_wsgi creator builds Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for Python web apps
summary: Graham Dumpleton, who created mod_wsgi, is building Muru, a Rust-based server for running WSGI and ASGI Python apps, with AI assistance. He is documenting the design in detail in a public blog series. This is a development project, not a security incident.
